summary: Defines the file layouts used by the ISI TOPS-20 implementation of the Mail Transfer Protocol. It is a companion to the main implementation description.

subtitle: The file formats for ISI TOPS-20's MTP mail system.

tldr.problem: Mail creation systems need a standard way to pass unsent messages to the Mail Transfer Protocol system on TOPS-20.
tldr.mechanism: Two files are used: a control file containing source and destination addresses, and a mail file containing the message text. The control file points to the mail file and lists all recipients.
tldr.outcome: This interface eliminated the need to create one copy of each message per recipient, simplifying mail system design.

facts.label: Control file format
facts.value: ASCII text with FILE:, FROM:, and TO: lines

today: RFC 785 describes a historical file format for TOPS-20 MTP systems. This implementation is specific to that platform and era, and is no longer in general use.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 785 defines the file interface between mail creation systems (such as MM or HERMES) and the Mail Transfer Protocol (MTP) on ISI's TOPS-20 system. It describes the file structures and naming conventions that allow these systems to exchange outgoing mail.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo describes how mail-writing programs talk to mail-sending programs using files on the TOPS-20 computer.

sections.title: Control and Mail Files
sections.content:
The interface uses two files per message. The control file, named ^V[--UNSENT-MAIL-CONTROL--^V].MTP.-1, is an ASCII text file containing routing information: a FILE: line pointing to the mail text file, a FROM: line with the source address, and one or more TO: lines with destination addresses. The mail file contains the message headers and body conforming to RFC 733 format.

This two-file structure replaces the earlier method where mail creation systems created one separate file for each recipient, named with the mailbox and host of that recipient.
sections.plainLanguage: The control file is like a delivery label listing all the addresses, and the mail file is the actual letter. Both point to each other.

sections.title: Addressing and Paths
sections.content: Source and destination paths in the control file use angle brackets and are identical to the paths described in the MTP specification (RFC 780). The path format includes all routing information needed for MTP to relay the message to its destinations. Both the source address and all destination addresses are specified in a single control file, regardless of how many recipients the message has.
sections.plainLanguage: Addresses are written with angle brackets, like <person@computer>, and MTP knows how to deliver to each one listed in the control file.
